[NEWLINE]Can only be trained while at war with a major civilization.
[NEWLINE]You already have {1_Num} of this unit, the most you can buy.
[NEWLINE]Requires at least {1_Num} {1_Num: plural 1?Tenet; other?Tenets;} of this Ideology.
Lost civilizations live on in your empire: {1_Buildings} now replace their standard counterparts.
{2_Building:textkey} will restore the unique buildings of civilizations absent from this world: {1_Buildings}.
Your {1_Unit:textkey} was struck by {2_Hazard:textkey} and lost {3_Num} HP.
{2_Hazard:textkey} struck an enemy {1_Unit:textkey} in your territory.
Pillage an adjacent enemy Improvement from aboard ship without disembarking. Costs one pillage move, free for Units that pillage without expending Movement.
No adjacent enemy Improvement to raid, or no Movement left.
Spoils: {1_Num} [ICON_GOLD] banked from pillaging. Paid out as [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture when this Unit enters your territory.
This [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Route is protected by a nearby escort and cannot be plundered.
Pillaged improvements cannot be repaired in enemy territory.
{@1_UnitName} returned with Spoils: +{2_Num} [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production in {@3_CityName} and +{4_Num} [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
With {4_CivName} eliminated, {@2_ReligionName} now belongs to {1_CivName}, who holds its Holy City of {@3_CityName}.
With {3_CivName} eliminated, {@1_ReligionName} is now yours, because you hold its Holy City of {@2_CityName}. You gain its Founder Belief, and your Great Prophets can enhance and spread it.
With its founder eliminated, {@1_ReligionName} now belongs to an unknown civilization that holds its Holy City.
Your vassal {1_CivName} has sent you a {2_UnitName}.
Your master has imposed its Ideology on your empire, which falls into Anarchy for {1_Num} {1_Num: plural 1?turn; other?turns;}.
Your {1_SpyRank} {2_SpyName} could not steal a technology in {3_CityName}, but gathered intelligence worth {5_Num}[ICON_RESEARCH] toward your current research.
An unidentified spy tried to steal technological secrets from {1_CityName} but only got away with some research notes.
{TXT_KEY_GRAMMAR_UPPER_A_AN << {1_CivAdj}} spy tried to steal technological secrets from {2_CityName} but only got away with some research notes.
Your pantheon has gained an additional belief.
{1_CivName} {1: plural 1?has; 2?have;} added another belief to their pantheon.
An unknown civilization has added another belief to their pantheon.

Click to jump to the trade unit.[NEWLINE]Ctrl+Click to recall it: the route ends at once and the unit is back in its home city next turn, free to be sent elsewhere. The cost is one turn of that route's yields.[NEWLINE][ICON_INFINITY] marks a route that runs until you recall it.
[ICON_INFINITY] This Trade Route runs until you recall the unit in the Trade Route Overview.
There {1: plural 1?is; other?are;} {1} possible trade route{1: plural 2?s;} from {2_CityName}
{1_CivName} has discovered {2_Num} technologies that you do not know.
You are receiving {1_Num} [ICON_RESEARCH] Science on this route due to your Cultural Influence over them.
You have discovered {1_Num} technologies that {2_CivName} does not know.
They are receiving {1_Num} [ICON_RESEARCH] Science on this route due to their Cultural Influence over you.
In the ruins you find the treasures of an ancient empire!
You have found a secret religious community. The preacher foretells the arrival of a Great Prophet.
You have found an ancient oracle. The priestess has blessed you with a divine revelation.
You have found cultural artifacts which awe your citizens!
{1_perTurn:number "#.##"} [ICON_TOURISM] from Trade Routes established with this city
The City-State of {1_MinorName} thanks you for slaying an enemy unit that was threatening them!
Unit must be at full Health.
This order will expend the Unit, giving you a large amount of [ICON_GOLD] Gold as well as spreading [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism to all civilizations.
Unit must be inside your own territory.
This order will consume the unit and cause 2 turns of Anarchy in all civilizations you are at war with. If at peace, it will cause 1 turn of Anarchy in all other civilizations.
{@1_CivName} has launched a Cyber Attack against your civilization and thrown it into Anarchy.
Unit must be at full Health.
This order will expend the Unit, granting an additional trade route slot.
Unit must be in or adjacent to one of your cities and there must be a valid Corporation slot available in a commercial building.

This command instructs the [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Great Merchant[ENDCOLOR] to found a [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporation[ENDCOLOR] in the city of {2_CityName}. The Corporation will be registered in the {1_BuildingName}, occupying a dedicated corporate slot.
The unit must be on a [COLOR_YELLOW]Tribal Settlement[ENDCOLOR] located in neutral territory and not adjacent to an owned tile.

This command instructs the [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Great Emissary[ENDCOLOR] to establish a [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]City-State[ENDCOLOR] at its current location. The [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Emissary[ENDCOLOR] is consumed during the process.
Unit must be in owned territory to use this ability.

Your {1_UnitType} returns from a journey to distant lands with [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{2_ResourceNames}[ENDCOLOR], a luxury found nowhere on this map. You gain [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{3_Num}[ENDCOLOR] copies of it.

Something already lies beneath your new {1_ImprovementName}, so no luxury could surface there. Instead you gain [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]1[ENDCOLOR] copy of [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{2_ResourceName}[ENDCOLOR], which your empire keeps for good.

If the Unit is in owned territory, this order will expend the Unit, granting you two free copies of a Luxury Resource not available on this map. These Resources will not appear on the map, but can be traded to other civilizations.
Unit must be at full Health.
This order will consume the unit and grant a free [ICON_CULTURE] Social Policy.
Unit must be in neutral territory.
This order will teleport the Unit to your Capital.
Must be on terrain suitable for the target unit. [NEWLINE]LAND UNIT: Land OR Coastal Water. [NEWLINE]NAVAL UNIT: Water OR Coastal City. [NEWLINE]Needs enough [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
Convert this unit. Costs [ICON_GOLD] Gold; free when changing back into a unit that can be trained.
Your new Defensive Pact has joined you into a larger defensive alliance. You now also hold Defensive Pacts with: {1_CivList}.[NEWLINE]An attack on any member will bring you to war on their behalf.
I admire your military prowess. Shall we make a Defensive Pact?
We should form an alliance, in order to bring ruin to our enemies. Do you want to make a Defensive Pact?
Our enemies surround us. If we do not work together, we will surely perish. Would you like to make a Defensive Pact?
The tyrants of the world would tremble at our feet, if only we were allied. Do you see the value in a Defensive Pact?

Hand this [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Missionary[ENDCOLOR] over to automation: it travels to the cities it judges best and spreads its religion there on its own. It stays automated until you cancel the automation or give it a new order.
Automation is not available for this unit right now.

Hand this [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Archaeologist[ENDCOLOR] over to automation: it seeks out Antiquity Sites and excavates them on its own. It stays automated until you cancel the automation or give it a new order.
Automation is not available for this unit right now.
Because {1_CivName:textkey} was captured, your gifted {2_Unit} was returned to you.
You have circled the globe! Your civilization may now establish an additional [ICON_INTERNATIONAL_TRADE] Trade Route.
Allows cities to work an additional ring of tiles.

Ask this leader to join you in a war against another civilization.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]If they agree to fight now, you both declare war at once and neither of you can make peace with the target for 15 turns. They may instead promise to join in 10 turns, when they will ask you to start the war together; turning them down then counts as a broken promise.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The plan is called off if either of you denounces or declares war on the other, or if peace is made with the target.
May not attack this player until the Industrial Era: a Religion founded on one side of this war forbids war against those who follow it. The ban also covers Defensive Pact partners and vassals.
They cannot declare war on you until the Industrial Era: a founded Religion binds you both.
Clicking this button will [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]DENOUNCE[ENDCOLOR] the other player.

How this leader rates the current deal. A positive number favors them and a negative number favors you; they turn down any deal that favors you. 'Will Not Trade!' means at least one item in the deal is off the table for them.
Their Net Gain: Will Not Trade!
What this leader thinks the items in this peace deal are worth. 'Will Not Trade!' means they refuse to give or accept at least one of the items.
The most this leader is prepared to give up to end the war. If the terms to the left are worth more than this, they will refuse.
The least this leader will accept from you to end the war. If the terms to the left are worth less than this, they will refuse.
In a peace deal only the surrendering side hands over items. Nothing can be added for the winning side to give.
{1_Civ} will only capitulate to a civilization that holds its original capital, {2_City}.
{1_Civ} will only capitulate to a civilization that holds one of its former capitals.
{1_PlayerName} has freed {2_CityName} and restored {3_CivAdj} sovereignty. Reborn in its original capital, the {4_CivName} pledges itself to {1_PlayerName} as a voluntary vassal.
If either player is attacked, the other immediately and automatically declares war on the attacker. The pact lasts {1_Num} turns.
Acquiring this Resource would start "We Love the King Day" in:
Ask a civilization that has a Declaration of Friendship with you for help. Unlike a demand, asking a friend does not harm your relations.
Demand tribute from this civilization. Whatever their answer, they will hold the demand against you.
May not negotiate peace right now: they are locked into this war for a number of turns.
May not negotiate peace with this player due to a game option or special rule.
[COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]They are bound to us by a Defensive Pact![ENDCOLOR]

The progress of {1_TeamName} towards a {2_VictoryName} victory has been reset!
Other civilizations that have pledged to protect this City-State. Attacking it or demanding tribute from it will anger them.
Being this City-State's Ally for {2_NumTurns} consecutive turns unlocks the {1_WonderName} World Wonder for you.
As the first great empire to reach them, you are presented with a treasured work of art worth [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumCulture} [ICON_CULTURE] Culture[ENDCOLOR].
No outsider has visited them before, and their priests bless your people with [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumFaith} [ICON_PEACE] Faith[ENDCOLOR].
Honored to be found first by your great empire, they present you with [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumGold} [ICON_GOLD] Gold[ENDCOLOR].
Your arrival coincides with their harvest festival, and they send [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumFood} [ICON_FOOD] Food[ENDCOLOR] to one of your cities.
Their veteran warriors share hard-won lessons with the unit that discovered them, which gains [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumXP} Experience[ENDCOLOR].
They welcome you with songs and stories, a gift worth [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumCulture} [ICON_CULTURE] Culture[ENDCOLOR].
Their priests teach your envoys some of their rites, granting you [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumFaith} [ICON_PEACE] Faith[ENDCOLOR].
They welcome your envoys with a purse of [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumGold} [ICON_GOLD] Gold[ENDCOLOR].
They send [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumFood} [ICON_FOOD] Food[ENDCOLOR] to one of your cities as a sign of goodwill.
Their veteran warriors share a few lessons with the unit that discovered them, which gains [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]{1_NumXP} Experience[ENDCOLOR].
Sadly, they have no gift to spare.

They have no gift to spare, but meeting {2: gender *:an?an; other?a;} {2_Personality} City-State still raises your [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT][ICON_INFLUENCE] Influence with them by {1_NumFriendship}[ENDCOLOR].
You have a unit ready for upgrade

{1_CityName} can no longer work on {2_BldgName}. The lost [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production has been converted into {3_NumGold}[ICON_GOLD] Gold, {4_NumCulture}[ICON_CULTURE] Culture, and {5_NumProduction}[ICON_PRODUCTION] overflow Production.

Multiplayer desync detected; the game was resynchronized. If it keeps happening, please send the host's and your own net_message_debug.log, SapiensMod.log and Lua.log (Documents\My Games\Sid Meier's Civilization 5\Logs), copied before restarting the game.

The game is close to the memory limit of 32-bit programs, a limit of the game itself, not of your computer. You can usually keep playing for a while, but later saves may need lower graphics settings to load. Save now, lower leader quality, shadows, terrain detail and anti-aliasing, and quit to the desktop before you next load.

The game is close to the memory limit of 32-bit programs, a limit of the game itself, not of your computer. You can usually keep playing for a while, but later saves may stop loading. Save now, and quit to the desktop and start the game fresh before you next load; DirectX 11 and a lower resolution give a little more room.

Gaia's Core Mod is enabled, but its DLL did not load, so most of its features, and those of mods built on it such as Sapiens, will not work in this game.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Mac and Linux versions of the game cannot load DLL mods. On Linux, run the Windows version through Steam Play (Proton). On Windows, make sure no other DLL mod is enabled, then restart the game.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Mods whose names start with + or = do not need the DLL.
You have acquired {1_CityName}. What would you like to do with this City?

You have pillaged {1_Num} [ICON_GOLD], {2_Num} [ICON_CULTURE], and {3_Num} [ICON_GREAT_WORK] from the capture of {@4_CityName}!!! Great Works with no free slot in this City were moved to your nearest City that has one.
Open the Promotion Tree to view this unit’s current and available promotions.
Promotions this unit has already earned (excludes those from unique traits or wonders).
Promotions currently available for this unit to select.
Promotions not yet available for this unit.
Click to toggle between this unit's promotion tree and the tree organized by combat class. Shortcut key: 'S'.
{1_LeaderName} has swapped your Great Work "{2_Work1Name}" for the Great Work "{3_Work2Name}."
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]You sent emissaries to them in goodwill.[ENDCOLOR]
Your emissary was warmly received. Their leader thinks better of you now.
The unit must be inside the borders of another civilization at peace with you. Civilizations led by a human player cannot receive one, and each civilization accepts only a limited number from you.

If the unit is inside the borders of another civilization you are at peace with, this order will expend the unit. That civilization's leader will think better of you from then on. Each later mission to the same civilization counts for less, and declaring war on them cancels the effect.

Send this land Unit by sea to a tile in or next to another of your Seaports on the same sea. It waits in port without orders during the voyage and lands at the start of your turn 2 turns later, with full Movement and healed as if it had rested. If an Airlift or a Paradrop can reach the tile, the Unit goes there at once instead.
The Unit must be a land Unit that has not moved this turn, in or next to one of your Cities with a Seaport, and you need another Seaport on the same sea. A blockaded port cannot be used.
{@1_UnitName} sets sail for {@2_CityName} and will land there on turn {3_Num}.
In transit to {@1_CityName}: lands on turn {2_Num}.
The sealift of {@1_UnitName} was called off: a port can no longer be used or there is no safe tile to land on.
{@1_CityName} has been chartered as a new City-State. It starts allied to you.
No new City-State could be chartered, so {@1_CityName} was founded as a Puppet City.
